headline: U.S. crude oil price falls to $87 a barrel
summary: Crude oil prices slipped to $87 a barrel as analysts project a fourth-quarter surplus in global supply, driven by recovering exports from the Middle East.

headline: Five EU states back Rwanda migrant deportation hub
summary: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands announced a joint “return hub” in Rwanda for asylum seekers whose applications have been rejected, aiming to curb irregular migration.

headline: US hyperscaler datacenters emit as much CO₂ as Denmark
summary: Research shows the rapid build-out of large AI-focused datacenters in the United States generated about 25.7 million tonnes of carbon dioxide, roughly matching Denmark’s annual emissions.

headline: SpaceX Starship launch succeeds amid tech sell-off
summary: SpaceX achieved a mostly successful Starship launch, reinforcing its lead in the space race even as a broader technology market downturn weighed on its share price.

headline: Prediction market odds rise for Tesla-SpaceX merger
summary: Odds that Tesla and SpaceX will merge by April 2027 climbed to 62% from 27% after speculation intensified about a possible integration of the two Elon Musk-led companies.

headline: US Justice Department warns Warren over future investigations
summary: The Justice Department sent a letter to the likely Senate Banking Committee chair, cautioning Democrats about plans for new investigations following their recent electoral gains.

headline: Analysts flag 13 S&P 500 stocks could jump 70% next year
summary: Consensus earnings estimates have risen for a group of S&P 500 companies, especially semiconductor makers, leading analysts to project potential gains of up to 70% over the coming year.

headline: US homeowners launch property-tax revolt over rising costs
summary: A growing movement of American homeowners is pushing for cuts to property taxes as they grapple with escalating housing expenses, seeking relief through legislative action.

headline: Robert Pattinson announced as new James Bond
summary: British actor Robert Pattinson has been confirmed as the next James Bond, taking over the role after Daniel Craig’s departure.

headline: Trump backs Jensen Huang return as Nvidia CEO amid scandal
summary: Former President Donald Trump said he would welcome Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia chief, dismissing the company’s scandal as not a national-security risk, while the Commerce Department moves to close a data-center export loophole.

headline: Grammy nominations feature Tame Impala and Raye among women-dominated list
summary: The 2027 Grammy nominations were announced with a strong female presence, led by Raye and Rosalía. Australian act Tame Impala secured a spot among the few male nominees, while legends like Dolly Parton received posthumous nods.

headline: US colleges face financial strain as international enrolments plunge
summary: Higher tuition costs and tighter immigration rules have caused a sharp drop in international student numbers at US universities, threatening the financial stability of many campuses that rely on overseas tuition revenue.

headline: Queensland businessmen plead guilty to selling Russian jet engines to China
summary: Two businessmen from Queensland were convicted of attempting to export Russian fighter-jet engines to China, breaching export controls. Their case was highlighted alongside former US President Trump’s comments on Putin’s stance in the Ukraine conflict.

headline: FDA rejects Summit Therapeutics’ lung-cancer drug pending survival data
summary: The US Food and Drug Administration declined to approve Summit Therapeutics’ lung-cancer candidate, stating the drug must demonstrate an overall survival benefit before it can be cleared for use.

headline: Jefferies fund relaxes lending checks for iron-ore traders amid fraud accusations
summary: Jefferies-backed fund Point Bonita eased verification requirements for iron-ore traders, allowing Glencore to bypass invoice checks from Radiant World and Sapphire despite ongoing fraud allegations.

headline: Two men charged after van runs over man in Birmingham flags incident
summary: Police charged two suspects in connection with a May incident in Birmingham where a man was struck by a van after flags were removed from a lamp-post, leaving him with leg injuries.

headline: Novo’s Wegovy trial shows weight loss in six-year-olds
summary: A Novo Nordisk trial found that the Wegovy injection helped nearly 80% of children as young as six lose more than 10% of their BMI, marking the first data on the drug’s effect in under-12s.

headline: NYC mayor disbands controversial police strategic response group
summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced the dissolution of the Strategic Response Group, a police unit criticized for aggressive tactics against protesters, and introduced a new community-safety division.

headline: Warren Buffett donates $5.5 billion in charitable giving
summary: Berkshire Hathaway chairman emeritus Warren Buffett announced a $5.5 billion donation in his Thanksgiving letter, saying kindness compounds. He still holds 182,140 Class A shares, valued at roughly $162 billion.

headline: Bitcoin falls below $62,000 after liquidation cascade
summary: Bitcoin slipped under $62,000 as a wave of long-position liquidations hit the market, pushing the cryptocurrency below key technical support levels before a modest rebound.

headline: Estonia shuts Russia border crossings after alleged drone factory arson
summary: The Estonian government ordered the closure of all Russia border crossings, blaming a recent attempted arson at a drone factory on Russian actors, a claim the Kremlin denies.

headline: NSW bill to boost Mount Pleasant coal output raises corruption concerns
summary: A New South Wales bill that would allow MACH Energy to increase production at the Mount Pleasant coal mine is being criticised for giving the resources minister sweeping powers that could create a serious corruption risk.

headline: Home insurance premiums in Australia up nearly 50% in five years
summary: Australian homeowners face premiums that have risen almost 50% over the past five years, with some policies costing up to $8,000 a year, forcing many to choose between coverage and unaffordability.

headline: New photos reveal life in 1946 Pilbara strike camps
summary: A collection of photographs uncovered beneath a wardrobe provides a rare glimpse of daily life in the Aboriginal workers' strike camps of Pilbara in 1946, eight decades after the protest.

headline: UK warns mushroom grow kits may spread invasive species
summary: British horticultural experts have advised against using popular golden oyster mushroom grow kits, classifying them as high-risk invasive species that could damage native woodlands.

headline: Major NFT marketplace announces closure after five-year boom
summary: A leading non-fungible token marketplace is shutting down, marking the end of a five-year cycle that saw rapid growth followed by a bust, and highlighting the risks of speculative digital-asset investments.

headline: Brisbane attracts more visitors while resident satisfaction falls
summary: Tourism and cultural events are drawing increasing numbers of visitors to inner-city Brisbane, but local residents report declining satisfaction due to concerns over housing affordability and safety.

headline: Ineos settles dispute with Ben Ainslie over America’s Cup yacht
summary: Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos Group has reached an out-of-court settlement with Sir Ben Ainslie, ending a legal fight over the £180 million yacht built for the 2024 America’s Cup. The agreement resolves claims that Ineos refused to return the vessel, avoiding a trial scheduled for next year.

headline: Andy Burnham launches fund to restore UK lidos
summary: UK Labour leader Andy Burnham announced a public fund to refurbish threatened outdoor swimming pools, known as lidos. The initiative follows a surge in demand for open-air swimming and aims to preserve historic art-deco facilities built in the 1930s.

headline: Israeli opposition leader calls for probe into PM’s office
summary: Gadi Eisenkot, the main challenger to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, has demanded an investigation into the Prime Minister’s Office after allegations that it fabricated claims of electoral fraud. The request adds pressure ahead of upcoming elections.

headline: David Beckham’s brand sues over unauthorised fragrance sales
summary: DB Ventures, the company owned by former footballer David Beckham, has filed a lawsuit against a distributor after its fragrance range was found for sale in Poundland and a petrol-station bargain bin, which the brand says were not authorised retail channels.

headline: American basketball player arrested with 75 lb of marijuana in Nigeria
summary: U.S. basketball player Greene Da’monte Khiree was detained at Lagos airport after customs officials discovered approximately 33.9 kg of marijuana in his luggage. Nigerian authorities said the alleged smuggling offence carries a life-sentence.

headline: Ukraine strikes Kerch bridge linking Crimea to Russia
summary: Ukrainian forces hit the Kerch bridge with a kamikaze drone, damaging an arch and temporarily halting road traffic. The attack, part of a broader drone barrage, left thousands of drivers stranded and underscored the bridge’s strategic importance.

headline: Exiled Guatemalan Nobel laureate’s ashes returned home
summary: The ashes of Miguel Ángel Asturias, a Guatemalan poet, writer and diplomat who died in exile in 1974, have been repatriated to Guatemala, allowing a symbolic homecoming for the Nobel-prize-winning author.

headline: Man sentenced for attempted murder of three children
summary: Riad Bouchaker received a prison term after being convicted of the attempted murder of three children in November 2023. The court handed down the sentence following a trial that highlighted the severity of the offence.

headline: Analysis: Putin, Trump and Xi cannot form a new ‘big three’
summary: A Financial Times commentary argues that the leaders of the United States, China and Russia are unable to dominate global affairs as a unified bloc, citing structural, strategic and domestic constraints that prevent them from carving up the world together.

headline: Nvidia shares fall after US restricts chip access to China
summary: Nvidia’s stock continued to decline after the US Commerce Department announced a rule limiting China’s remote access to advanced chips. The move follows harsh comments from the US government about the chipmaker’s ties to China, adding pressure on the company’s share price.

headline: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal after sexual assault conviction
summary: French actor Gérard Depardieu has withdrawn his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a Paris film set. In a written statement he accepted the verdict and apologised to the victims, confirming the court’s original ruling.

headline: Pakistan floods linked to intensified monsoon rainfall
summary: University lecturer Imran Lodhi describes how climate-driven intense monsoon rains caused devastating floods in Dera Ghazi Khan, Pakistan, displacing families and prompting urgent relief efforts.

headline: Rising shipping costs could limit holiday inventory
summary: Transport executives say higher freight rates are prompting retailers to curb stock of big-ticket holiday items, making some products harder to find for shoppers.

headline: UK’s oldest renewable projects set for £9bn subsidy windfall
summary: Analysis shows that legacy wind and solar farms in Britain could receive nearly £9 billion in payments next year as market prices surge, prompting calls to reform the subsidy scheme.

headline: Eurovision Asia footage edited in Malaysia over LGBTQ content
summary: The European Broadcasting Union says it will write to the Asian contest licence holder after Malaysia’s TV3 cut drag and gay jury footage from the first Eurovision Asia broadcast.

headline: Teen AFL hopeful Lucas Robinson eyes legend’s footsteps ahead of draft
summary: Prospective draftee Lucas Robinson reveals the Australian Football League great he wants to emulate as he prepares for this week’s national draft.

headline: Xi, Trump and Putin to meet in Shenzhen for trilateral talks
summary: China, the United States and Russia will hold a first-of-its-kind trilateral meeting in Shenzhen during the APEC summit, with leaders Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin expected to discuss world-peace topics such as denuclearisation.

headline: Israeli military uploads 3.5 million photos to Amazon cloud for facial-recognition analysis
summary: Leaked documents reveal Israel moved millions of images of Palestinians to Amazon’s cloud platform to use its facial-recognition tools during the Gaza conflict.

headline: Investor warns fame can undermine tech founders at Nvidia and Tesla
summary: A prominent shareholder argues that the celebrity status of CEOs at Nvidia and Tesla can negatively affect both personal lives and company performance.

headline: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 17 dead
summary: Separate attacks in KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng have killed 17 people, highlighting the country’s ongoing struggle with violent crime.

headline: Robert Irwin and sprinter Gout among Queensland’s Australian of the Year nominees
summary: Conservationist Robert Irwin and 2024 sprint champion Gout Gout join two other Queensland advocates as finalists for the state’s Australian of the Year awards.

headline: Two passengers trapped atop Perth ferris wheel after operator leaves early
summary: WorkSafe will investigate after a Perth ferris wheel operator departed before the ride finished, leaving two paying riders stranded at the top.

headline: NSW inquest hears birth keeper told mother of deceased baby to ‘go home and rest’
summary: Coroner’s court hears that a birth keeper advised a pregnant woman, whose baby later died, to return home despite urgent medical advice to seek emergency care.

headline: Four-year-old injured after car crashes into Perth daycare fence
summary: A vehicle struck the fence of a daycare centre in Perth, causing injuries to a four-year-old boy. Emergency services attended the scene and the child was taken for medical treatment. No further details on the driver or cause were provided.

headline: Inquest opened into police shooting of 16-year-old in Perth car park
summary: A coronial inquest has begun into the fatal police shooting of a 16-year-old boy, described as radicalised, at a Bunnings car park in Perth. The inquiry will examine the circumstances surrounding the incident and the actions of the officer involved.

headline: NSW Premier Minns drops underquoting reforms amid housing slump backlash
summary: New South Wales Premier Chris Minns has shelved proposed underquoting legislation that would have forced real-estate agents to disclose price expectations to buyers. The decision follows a slowdown in the housing market and strong opposition from Sydney agents.

headline: Cape Town baboon relocation to sanctuary sparks protests
summary: Authorities in Cape Town began moving a troop of 44 baboons from Simon’s Town to a wildlife sanctuary, prompting demonstrators to block the transport. Officials say the relocation is needed to reduce human-wildlife conflict, while locals oppose the capture.

headline: Queensland police review use of unofficial AI-powered app
summary: Queensland Police are examining the deployment of an unofficial AI-driven application used by frontline officers after concerns were raised about its governance and data handling. The review follows broader scrutiny of AI tools in public sector operations.

headline: Opinion piece links wartime leaks to technology insiders
summary: A commentary argues that recent leaks of sensitive information may be traced to technology experts, suggesting a new dimension to espionage in modern conflicts.

headline: WA Police investigate complaints about Labor MP’s alleged debts
summary: Western Australian police have received complaints concerning alleged debts of Labor MP Jagadish Krishnan. The force confirmed the matters are under investigation.

headline: Inquest probes deaths of four babies born at home in northern NSW
summary: A coronial inquest is examining the circumstances surrounding the deaths of four infants born at home in northern New South Wales, including a mother’s fear of being forced into a caesarean section if she sought hospital care.

headline: Conjoined twin girls born in remote PNG, possible treatment in Australia
summary: Medical teams in a remote part of Papua New Guinea have delivered conjoined twin girls, marking the country’s second such case in just over a year. Authorities are exploring the possibility of transferring the infants to Australia for specialised care.

headline: European banks adopt AI to cut routine work but profit impact unclear
summary: Banks across Europe are deploying artificial intelligence to automate routine tasks, redeploy staff and recruit technical talent. While the technology promises efficiency gains, its effect on overall profitability remains uncertain.

headline: Rare EF1 tornado touches down in Delaware, causing property damage
summary: An EF1 tornado struck the Salem Woods neighbourhood of Newark, Delaware, damaging roofs, windows and a hotel sign, and overturning a semi-truck on I-95. No injuries or fatalities were reported.

headline: Swans players Heeney and Warner train after police clearance
summary: Sydney Swans stars Isaac Heeney and Chad Warner resumed training with teammates at Centennial Park following their clearance by police in connection with a hotel-room incident earlier this year.

headline: IMF chief warns AI-linked circular financing reaches $1 trillion
summary: Kristalina Georgieva said that circular financing for AI companies has grown to just over $1 trillion, with two-thirds in debt, as investor enthusiasm cools and global economic risks rise.

headline: Kangaroos credit doubters for World Cup triumph
summary: Australian rugby league stars said criticism of their abilities motivated the team, which went on to win the World Cup, highlighting the role of external scepticism in their success.

headline: Inquest begins into Queensland island fire deaths
summary: A coronial inquest has started into the blaze that killed a father and five children on a small Queensland island in 2023, seeking to determine the cause of the tragedy.

headline: Rugby Australia vows to fight players’ union legal challenge
summary: CEO Phil Waugh described the players’ union’s pay and conditions case as an aggressive, costly and avoidable legal battle, confirming Rugby Australia will defend the matter in court.

headline: Government scores poorly on every performance metric
summary: A new poll shows the current Australian government lagging on all measured performance indicators, with cost of living remaining the top concern for voters for the fifth consecutive year.

headline: Australia issues 30-year bonds as yields rise
summary: The Treasury launched a 30-year sovereign bond offering weeks after multi-decade high yields, attracting strong demand from global investors seeking long-term Australian debt.

headline: Metrics takes over distressed property assets
summary: Non-bank lender Metrics placed two property developers into receivership and listed a foreclosed retail strip for sale as defaults in the sector continue to rise.

headline: Severe weather forces 104 Sydney Airport flight cancellations
summary: Adverse weather conditions at Sydney Airport led to major delays and the cancellation of 104 flights, disrupting travel plans for thousands of passengers.

headline: UK, allies urge Israel to speed humanitarian aid to Gaza
summary: The United Kingdom, Australia, Canada and Italy called on Israeli authorities to allow rapid delivery of essential supplies, including 150,000 tents, to Gaza, saying restrictions at border crossings were hindering humanitarian assistance.

headline: Test cricket hopefuls miss final selection window
summary: With the New Zealand series squad imminent, prospects Sam Konstas and Jack Clayton failed to impress in the One-Day Cup, losing their last chance to earn a Test debut.

headline: Qantas travel disruptions strand island residents
summary: Passengers from Christmas Island and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands were left stranded on the mainland after Qantas cancelled multiple flights, prompting frustration among island communities.

headline: Opposition says key details omitted from Torrens-Darlington briefing
summary: Opposition figures claim the $15.4 billion Torrens to Darlington infrastructure project briefing left out critical information about a contractor later suspended over alleged bikie links.

headline: Judge’s Facebook posts not enough to overturn abuse ruling
summary: A court dismissed Stephen Fane Noga’s appeal against a verdict that found him liable for sexual abuse of a former student in the 1980s, ruling his social-media activity did not merit a reversal.

headline: Darwin Private Hospital to continue services after takeover delay
summary: The Northern Territory health minister urged patients to keep scheduled procedures at Darwin Private Hospital despite Calvary Health Care postponing its acquisition date.

headline: Greens weigh alternative 40% CGT discount proposal
summary: The Australian Greens are considering a simpler capital gains tax discount model proposed by teal MP Tim Spender, which could challenge the government’s current CGT reform plans.

headline: Lendlease faces investor scepticism over bond redemption plan
summary: Lendlease said its bond redemption was part of proactive capital management, but investors remain unconvinced. The company’s sticky covenant and unexpected move have raised concerns about its financial strategy and market confidence.

headline: Aboriginal teen becomes youngest world surfing champion
summary: An Australian Aboriginal teenager made history by winning the world surfing title, becoming the sport’s youngest champion. The achievement highlights the rising talent and diversity in Australian surfing.

headline: Authors and creators push back against AI copyright lobbying
summary: Australia’s government push to attract AI investment has sparked a campaign by authors, musicians and TV producers. The creative sector argues the policy favours AI firms and threatens copyright protections.

headline: Anti-hype pitch to back record-size IPO gains traction
summary: Dario Amodei’s low-profile approach is being used to support what could become the largest initial public offering. Clients have been told order sizes may be trimmed by about 40 per cent as the deal progresses.

headline: NSW police sexual misconduct allegations revealed in review
summary: A culture review of the NSW Police Force uncovered claims of sexual harassment and assault by officers against fellow uniformed staff. The findings have prompted calls for further investigation and reforms.

headline: Rare 16th-century ‘Book of Miracles’ to be auctioned for £1 million
summary: The ‘Book of Miracles’, a 16th-century manuscript depicting apocalyptic scenes such as five suns over Leipzig and blood rain in Rome, is set to be auctioned. Public institutions will have the first chance to bid.

headline: Sydney Airport flights disrupted after safety directive
summary: Airservices issued a safety directive that forced airlines to slow arrivals and increase spacing due to low cloud, resulting in 92 flight cancellations and 347 delays at Sydney Airport on Monday.

headline: Usman Khawaja discusses racism and mental health in cricket
summary: Australian cricketer Usman Khawaja opened up about experiencing racist stereotyping, his sense of belonging, and early mental-health struggles linked to cricket setbacks, expanding the conversation beyond the Sandpapergate controversy.

headline: UK Labour leader says Brexit has failed ahead of EU summit
summary: Labour Prime Minister Andy Burnham will argue at the upcoming UK-EU summit that Brexit “has not worked” and propose a new deal with the EU, claiming it could raise Britain’s GDP by 0.4 per cent. The comments come amid renewed debate over the post-Brexit relationship.

headline: Victorian town opposes AI data centre at former quarry
summary: Residents of Miners Rest, Victoria, are campaigning against a proposed AI data centre slated for the town’s old quarry, fearing it would disrupt their quiet rural lifestyle.

headline: James Packer’s large Nvidia stake highlighted amid scandal
summary: Billionaire James Packer’s significant investment in Nvidia has come under scrutiny, with reports noting his broader exposure to the tech giant through his Firmus holdings.

headline: Tasmanian author demands apology from premier over Christmas backlash
summary: Best-selling parenting author Biddulph has called on Tasmania’s premier to issue an unreserved apology after a social-media storm over the state’s Christmas celebrations.

headline: Humm faces board battle as director resigns and activist seeks seat
summary: Non-bank lender Humm is in turmoil after a director’s resignation and activist investor Jeremy Raper’s push for a board seat, intensifying a power struggle between founder Andrew Abercrombie and top shareholder.

headline: NSW anti-slavery commissioner refers labour hire syndicate crimes to police
summary: The NSW Anti-slavery Commissioner has referred allegations that labour hire syndicates kidnapped and blackmailed migrant workers to police, highlighting concerns over exploitation in the state’s labour market.

headline: NSW shelves new real estate advertising rules
summary: The NSW government has abandoned planned reforms that would have required property agents to display selling prices or price ranges, cancelling the changes a day before they were to take effect.

headline: PIMCO warns of sustained diesel shortage in Australia
summary: Asset manager PIMCO says the fallout from the US-Iran crisis could lead to a prolonged diesel crunch in Australia, urging an “all-energy” approach to meet rising demand.

headline: Severe thunderstorms bring snow-like hail to southern Queensland
summary: Heavy thunderstorms across southern Queensland produced hail up to 10 cm in size and wind gusts of 91 km/h, prompting warnings for residents in the affected areas.

headline: Jackdaw gas field receives UK government approval
summary: UK ministers have given the green light for gas production at the Jackdaw field, located 150 miles east of Aberdeen, after years of regulatory uncertainty.

headline: Court hears DNA link to Adelaide paediatrician murder suspect
summary: During a hearing, DNA matching murder-accused Kerem Aydin was reportedly found at the scene where Adelaide paediatrician Michael Yung was killed in 2023.

headline: Statue unveiled to honour Merle Thornton’s 1965 protest
summary: A new statue in Brisbane commemorates Merle Thornton, who chained herself to a bar in 1965 to protest the ban on women in Queensland public bars.

headline: Proposed on-shore gas bill faces constitutional challenge
summary: The coalition and Greens oppose a new bill that would require LNG exporters to supply a greater share of gas to Australian consumers, citing constitutional concerns.

headline: NRL highlights to be free for podcasters from 2028
summary: From 2028, podcasters covering the NRL will be allowed to use footage and highlight reels from Nine and Foxtel at no cost, subject to certain conditions.

headline: Beaconsfield miner Todd Russell remembered after death
summary: Former Beaconsfield miner Todd Russell was remembered for his humour and reflections on his funeral plans, recalling a previous burial he did not enjoy.

headline: Forrestania secures 72.5% stake in Zenith Minerals
summary: Forrestania Resources has completed a takeover offer, acquiring a 72.56 per cent controlling interest in Zenith Minerals. The deal advances Forrestania’s strategy to consolidate gold assets in Western Australia and brings Zenith under its operational umbrella.

headline: Australians at forefront of global AI safety efforts
summary: Dozens of Australians have relocated to San Francisco to work for leading AI labs or the surrounding AI safety ecosystem. They are actively raising concerns about the risk of artificial intelligence systems becoming uncontrolled.

headline: Gateway Mining reports high-grade gold find at Yandal project
summary: Gateway Mining announced a shallow, high-grade gold discovery at its Yandal project near Wiluna, Western Australia. Recent reverse-circulation drilling returned 11 metres at 4.5 g/t gold from 89 metres depth, confirming a new mineralised system.

headline: Westfield seeks new anchors as David Jones administrators meet creditors
summary: The owner of Westfield shopping centres has intensified pressure on administrators of David Jones, with meetings scheduled with creditors. Westfield is exploring replacement tenants for the department store’s locations across its Australian malls.

headline: UK ministers warned weakening EV targets would hurt car industry
summary: Experts told UK ministers that diluting the zero-emission vehicle mandate would slow market growth, raise costs for consumers and undermine the country's net-zero objectives, potentially harming the domestic automotive sector.

headline: Home Office criticised for attempting to cancel Andreas Malm online talk
summary: The Home Office faced accusations of trying to block an online event featuring climate academic Andreas Malm. Hackney mayor Shadwell decried the move as an assault on free speech after the talk proceeded despite warnings.

headline: England plans reforms to expand appeals for special-needs support
summary: Proposed changes to England’s special-needs education system could give families new routes to appeal for additional school support, including ombudsman reviews, amid criticism that current reforms dilute legal protections.

headline: Police shooting of 16-year-old extremist and trial of ex-officer draws scrutiny
summary: A coronial inquest heard that 16-year-old James Hollands, who sent a jihad-related text, was shot by police after a knife attack. Former NSW police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon, charged with double murder, faced cross-examination and later re-examination by his own barrister during the trial.

headline: Allens bolsters M&A practice hiring Hamilton Locke senior partner
summary: Allens has expanded its mergers and acquisitions team, bringing in senior partner Hamilton Locke from Hamilton Locke. The move follows the firm’s ongoing effort to grow its M&A and capital markets capabilities.

headline: Travis Auld steps down as Australian Grand Prix Corp CEO
summary: Travis Auld has resigned as chief executive of the Australian Grand Prix Corporation. He will not disclose his next employer or the location of his new role, and his departure comes ahead of the upcoming Formula 1 season.

headline: Police release CCTV footage of fatal drive-by shooting
summary: Detectives from the Logan Criminal Investigation Branch have released CCTV footage showing a blue Mazda 2 near Bryants Road at the time of a fatal drive-by shooting. The video is being circulated to aid the investigation and encourage anyone with information to come forward.

headline: Report flags dysfunction at Serpentine Jarrahdale council
summary: An independent monitor’s report on the Shire of Serpentine Jarrahdale highlights concerns over councillor behaviour and psychosocial safety. The findings suggest systemic issues within the council and call for reforms to improve governance and staff wellbeing.

headline: Health Minister Butler urges states to allow puberty blockers
summary: Health Minister Mark Butler has challenged states and territories that have banned puberty blockers for children to follow new national guidelines. He says the guidelines are based on medical consensus and that denying access could harm young people’s health.

headline: EU envoy urges Australian government to back trade pact
summary: The new EU ambassador said the bloc would consider climate-assurance requests if the Australian government proposes a win-win trade deal. He described the potential agreement as a “bloody good deal” and urged the Coalition to support the negotiations.

headline: AFR launches indices to broaden ASX investment view
summary: The Australian Financial Review has introduced a suite of indices designed to give a wider economic perspective on ASX opportunities. The launch is positioned as the next step in strengthening Australia’s capital-markets infrastructure and supporting investors.

headline: Lucy Wicks responds to stalking allegations by MP Taylor Martin
summary: NSW MP Taylor Martin accused former staffer Lucy Wicks of stalking him in a parliamentary speech. Wicks has now publicly replied, denying the claims and defending her conduct amid the political dispute.

headline: Rex posts losses as US owner fails to restore fleet
summary: Regional airline Rex reported a loss after its US owner, tasked with returning planes to service, has not added a single aircraft in almost a year. The ongoing issues raise concerns about the airline’s expansion plans.

headline: Mother describes grief after son killed by 16-year-old
summary: A mother recounted the “unbearable” grief she feels after her son, Jack Westren, who had a brain injury, was ambushed and murdered by a group of teenagers at Shellharbour Junction train station.

headline: Sam Walker to discuss PNG Chiefs move with club officials
summary: Off-contract Roosters centre Sam Walker will meet PNG Chiefs officials on Tuesday to explore a potential transfer to the expansion franchise, where he could partner with Jarome Luai in the halves.

headline: Witness testimony ends in Lamarre-Condon court case
summary: The Crown prosecutor concluded the witness testimony of Beau Lamarre-Condon, reading statements from Jesse Baird’s brother and Luke Davies’s mother relating to evidence given by the accused, marking the end of that phase of the trial.

headline: Critical Resources gains access to high-grade antimony prospect
summary: Critical Resources has secured ground access to its Mayview antimony-gold prospect in NSW, where rock chip samples returned 52.3 % antimony, located just 2.7 km from the existing Hillgrove mine.

headline: Ken Wyatt appointed WA’s first Indigenous governor
summary: Former federal minister Ken Wyatt, the first Indigenous Australian elected to the House of Representatives, has been named Western Australia’s inaugural Indigenous governor, marking a historic first for the state.

headline: Albanese urged to boycott photo with Putin at APEC
summary: Critics have called on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to avoid a photo-op with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit, warning it could normalise Russia’s standing and undermine Australia’s support for Ukraine.

headline: Judge rejects bid to keep Kmart child sex offender in prison
summary: A Queensland judge dismissed an application to keep a man convicted of child sexual offences at Kmart, allowing his release. The offender had lured a child from a mother in the toy aisle of a Westfield store in 2018. The decision follows legal arguments about his continued detention.

headline: Mother of five killed in Russell Island fire gives evidence at inquest
summary: A mother whose partner and five sons perished in a house fire on Russell Island has begun testifying at the inquest into the tragedy. She described the blaze as being everywhere and recounted the devastating loss of her family as investigators examine the cause of the fire.

headline: Australia joins US-led Pax Silica AI supply-chain pact
summary: Australia became a founding member of Pax Silica, a US-initiated alliance aimed at safeguarding AI supply chains from Chinese influence. The pact brings together seven countries to coordinate on rare-earth and semiconductor security, reflecting growing concerns over Beijing’s dominance in advanced technology components.

headline: Widow of Haiti’s assassinated leader registers for presidential race
summary: The wife of former Haitian president Jovenel Moïse, assassinated in 2021, has filed paperwork to run in the upcoming presidential election. Haiti has not held a national vote since the killing, and her candidacy marks a rare entry of a former first lady into the political arena.

headline: Independent MP Helen Haines discharged after hospitalisation
summary: Helen Haines, the independent MP who was attacked outside her office, has been released from hospital and entered the rehabilitation stage. She thanked supporters and donors for their messages and charity contributions. The attack resulted in double amputation of her legs, and she is now focusing on recovery.

headline: Barrenjoey tops broker survey as equities desks light up
summary: Barrenjoey Capital Partners was ranked first in the latest Peter Lee broker survey, outperforming peers across equity research and sales. The results highlight the firm’s strong performance on the Australian equities desk and its growing influence among institutional investors.

headline: Tax regulator pursues former KPMG manager over unauthorised GST refunds
summary: The Australian Taxation Office has launched action against Anthony George Confos, a former KPMG manager, for allegedly lodging unauthorised GST refunds and diverting nearly $1 million to personal accounts. The case underscores ongoing scrutiny of tax-avoidance schemes.

headline: Victorian premier says documents withheld from royal commission
summary: Premier Ben Carroll accused officials of withholding documents from the commission investigating the Big Build, while Health Minister Ingrid Stitt denied briefing claims. The dispute comes as the state government pushes free prenatal testing amid fears of an upcoming election loss.

headline: Former EY partner found to have promoted illegal tax schemes
summary: The Australian Taxation Office secured a court victory against former EY partner Peter White, who was found to have advised wealthy clients on unlawful tax structures. The ruling represents a significant enforcement action against professional misconduct in tax advisory services.

headline: UK ministers criticised for not knowing cost of NHS maternity repairs
summary: NHS chiefs warned that 43 percent of maternity and neonatal units in England fail to meet safety standards, accusing ministers of “gambling with safety” after admitting they lack knowledge of the repair costs for deteriorating facilities. The criticism highlights systemic infrastructure issues in the health system.

headline: Spain prepares for snap election that could bring far-right to power

The health ministry said the building housed surgical wards and intensive care units. Israel said it targeted Hamas fighters but offered no evidence.

headline: Ukraine reports Starshield satellite disruptions amid US-Russia talks
summary: Ukraine's president said recent speed restrictions on the Starshield military satellite network were hindering its defence efforts. The concerns were raised as US envoys arrived in Moscow for talks with President Putin, highlighting tensions over the technology's reliability in the ongoing conflict.

headline: Euclid mission maps 900 million galaxies in first data release
summary: The European Space Agency’s Euclid telescope released its inaugural dataset, revealing more than 900 million galaxies and about 15,000 gravitational-lensing candidates. The mission aims to produce the largest three-dimensional map of the universe, covering a third of the sky and tracing cosmic history back over 10 billion years.

headline: Five new miniature frog species discovered in eastern Himalayas
summary: Scientists have identified five previously unknown miniature frog species in the eastern Himalayas. The research suggests the frogs evolved alongside the uplift of the mountain range and the development of the Asian monsoon, highlighting the region’s unique biodiversity and geological history.

headline: College students rally across US campuses to back Starbucks boycott
summary: Students, staff and elected officials gathered at more than 40 US colleges to support the Starbucks Workers United boycott. The campaign seeks higher pay, a $17-hour minimum wage and a three-person staffing minimum, after five years of stalled contract talks with the coffee chain.

headline: John Kerry calls Trump ‘biggest loser’ over climate policy at COP31
summary: Speaking at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey, former US secretary of state John Kerry criticised former President Donald Trump for withdrawing the United States from climate commitments and handing the clean-energy lead to China, saying the move makes Trump the biggest loser in the climate arena.

headline: NHS England removes claim that 137 trusts benefit from Palantir AI
summary: After The Guardian exposed that only 29 NHS trusts were using Palantir’s AI data platform, NHS England deleted a website statement that had claimed 137 trusts were benefiting from the technology, acknowledging the earlier information was misleading.

headline: Maga architects blame Big Tech and AI data centres for US midterms loss
summary: The Heritage Foundation’s head argued that the Republican Party’s embrace of Silicon Valley and the fallout from the US-Iran war contributed to their defeat in the recent midterm elections, linking tech-sector policies to voter backlash.

headline: Ukraine says Starlink restrictions reinstated as US envoys arrive in Moscow
summary: Ukraine reported that restrictions on SpaceX’s Starlink service have been re-imposed, coinciding with a visit by US officials to Moscow. The move follows heightened tensions over Russian drone activity and diplomatic talks involving senior US figures.

headline: Greta Thunberg criticises Australia’s net-zero progress at COP31
summary: At the COP31 summit in Turkey, climate activist Greta Thunberg slammed Australia’s pace on net-zero emissions, describing it as slower than a snail. Her remarks drew a large media presence and prompted security guards to escort her from the stage.

headline: The return of the snatch-and-grab state
summary: A new historical analysis examines how modern governments employ confiscation tactics as a form of economic warfare, reviving the concept of the snatch-and-grab state in contemporary policy debates.

summary: Research suggests that the worst anti-AI trade policies by major chipmakers correlate with stronger performance of Indian stocks, highlighting a potential investment angle as global tech regulation intensifies.

headline: Italy proposes exit tax on emigrants’ capital gains
summary: The Italian government has introduced a tax targeting capital gains of wealthy emigrants, aiming to capture revenue from assets moved abroad. While theoretically sound, officials acknowledge challenges in practical implementation.

headline: Floreat gunman’s recording revealed at inquest into murders
summary: During the inquest into the deaths of Jennifer and Gretl Petelcyzc, evidence emerged that the Floreat shooter inadvertently recorded himself on the day of the attack, shedding new light on his interactions with police prior to the incident.

headline: Australia to spend $80m on workforce for AUKUS

summary: A government-run service provider disclosed that a cyber breach could have compromised personal information, including contact details, of individuals whose data it holds, prompting an investigation and advice for affected users to monitor for potential misuse.

headline: 72-year-old British woman missing from cruise ship in Atlantic
summary: A 72-year-old British passenger vanished from the Tui cruise liner as it sailed towards the Caribbean, prompting a search operation by authorities and the cruise line while family members appeal for information on her whereabouts.

summary: Candidates vying for mayoral office have suggested measures such as reducing council representatives, appointing an external auditor and tightening meeting discipline to address reports of a toxic, bullying culture within the local council and restore public confidence.

summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have moved into a new residence on a friend’s estate in the Cotswolds, following their return to the United Kingdom with their children earlier this year, according to reports.

summary: In a Melbourne court, prosecutors said Lamarre-Condon sent a message to alleged murder victim Jesse Baird stating he would not exist following their breakup. The exchange was presented as evidence of intimidation during the trial.

summary: Russian diesel shipments are set to double following the removal of US sanctions, according to the Financial Times. Analysts warn the surge may be short-lived as Ukraine resumes attacks on Russian refineries, potentially curbing export volumes.

summary: Paris and Berlin have signalled support for Pablo Hernández de Cos, Spain’s nominee for the European Central Bank presidency, aiming to create a package deal on central-bank leadership across the eurozone.

summary: In an Australian court, counsel argued that Stephen Roche, an Irish national who pleaded guilty to attempting to pervert the course of justice, should receive a lighter jail term for his role in helping a fugitive drug trafficker evade authorities.

summary: A new observatory, owned and operated by an Indigenous community in South Australia’s far west, has opened to showcase ancient star stories and promote cultural tourism, according to ABC News.

summary: The historic election of a Black senator from Mississippi, the first since former slave Blanche Bruce in 1874, was hailed by Democratic leaders as a milestone for representation and progress.

summary: Parts of Tasmania’s south-east commercial rock lobster and dive fisheries will be shut for three months to mitigate trade risks linked to antibiotic use in the salmon industry, the ABC reports.

summary: During a trial, the jury was shown months of text messages between Robert Crawford and his wife, including a message sent on the day she died, providing insight into their relationship before the fatal incident.

summary: In a rapid-fire interview, Jess Wilson, leader of the Victorian Opposition, revealed the people she would invite to a fantasy dinner and highlighted the key policy reforms she sees as most urgent for the state.
